articles.title: accesso on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's Lee Cowie outlines how AI and data analytics are pushing ticketing and in-park purchasing well beyond their traditional roles. For FEC operators, the piece highlights actionable ways to reduce guest friction and increase per-cap spending through smarter technology integration. This is a must-read as FEC venues face growing pressure to modernize their guest experience stack.

articles.title: Frictionless Guest Experiences: Why Removing Obstacles Drives Revenue
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's editorial frames the entire issue around a single insight: every obstacle between a guest and an experience costs operators money. The piece references ticketing, in-park purchasing, and immersive design as key friction points FEC operators should address. It serves as a strong strategic framework for operators planning capital or technology investments.

articles.title: Six Flags Fiesta Texas Breaks Ground on World's Longest Family Launch Coaster
articles.summary: Six Flags Fiesta Texas has broken ground on Werewolf Gorge, billed as the world's longest family launch coaster and the largest single-attraction investment in the park's history. The ride is scheduled to debut during the park's 35th anniversary season in 2027. The investment signals continued confidence in family-oriented thrill attractions as a driver of park differentiation.

articles.title: Premium Interactive Horror: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Bet Big on 'The Conjuring: Beyond Fear'
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences are investing in a premium-tier interactive horror experience tied to The Conjuring IP for the 2026 Halloween season. The piece explores how operators can balance crowd flow efficiency with high-value immersive add-ons during the fall season. FEC operators running haunted attractions or seasonal events will find the operational and pricing strategy insights especially relevant.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Bring AI-Powered Wave Tech to Surf Parks
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a strategic partnership combining customizable wave technology with AI-powered computer vision to create a more connected experience for surf park operators and guests. The integration, branded 'The Mixtape,' aims to personalize the surfing experience at scale. This partnership is a clear signal that surf park operators are moving toward data-driven, tech-enhanced attraction management.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands into Competitive Socializing with New Portfolio
articles.summary: Jora Vision is broadening its attraction design offering into competitive socializing, a fast-growing segment that overlaps heavily with FEC programming like mini golf, axe throwing, and skill-based gaming. The piece details how skill-based competitive experiences are being designed to appeal across age groups and visit frequencies. FEC operators looking to add or refresh competitive socializing concepts will find this directly applicable.

articles.title: Six Flags St. Louis Rebrands as Mid America Adventure
articles.summary: Six Flags St. Louis has officially changed its name to Mid America Adventure, unveiling a new logo and brand identity that emphasizes its regional identity and attraction diversity. The rebrand is part of broader positioning moves across the Six Flags portfolio following the Cedar Fair merger. FEC operators and investors should watch how large parks use rebranding to reset guest perception and compete for regional entertainment dollars.

articles.title: InPark Issue 111: Technology and the Frictionless Future of Theme Parks and FECs
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's latest issue centers on how technology is being used to deliver seamless, friction-free guest experiences across ticketing, attractions, and operations. Contributors include accesso, Jora Vision, and coverage of premium Halloween events, making this a comprehensive resource for FEC operators and suppliers. The issue also explores how AI-generated environments and smart design are reshaping what guests expect from entertainment venues.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Interactive Attraction Design
articles.summary: Alterface, a leading developer of interactive dark ride and shooting gallery systems, reflects on 25 years of creating immersive guest experiences for themed entertainment worldwide. The retrospective highlights design philosophy shifts from hardware-led to story-led interactivity, which is increasingly relevant for FEC operators adding dark rides or interactive attractions. Operators evaluating interactive attraction suppliers will benefit from understanding Alterface's long-term approach.

articles.title: Blue Sky Thinking in Attraction Design: How to Innovate Before Getting Practical
articles.summary: Creative leaders from Forrec and Moment Factory argue that the best attraction concepts emerge when designers resist operational constraints early in the process, allowing 'what-if' ideas to fully develop first. They also caution against technology driving design, advocating instead for tech as an invisible layer supporting storytelling and emotional connection. FEC operators and designers planning new attractions or refreshes will find this framework useful for internal ideation sessions.

articles.title: Family Coasters and Inclusive Attractions: Designing Rides the Whole Family Can Share
articles.summary: Theme park operators and manufacturers are increasingly investing in family coasters and attractions that eliminate height and age barriers, allowing parents, grandparents, and young children to ride together. The piece features case studies from ART Engineering, Lagoon Amusement Park, and Potts Park on how inclusive design is influencing attraction development. For FEC operators, this trend reinforces the growing commercial value of all-ages attractions that maximize group participation.

articles.title: Thorpe Park Debuts Pitch-Black Scare Maze for Fright Nights 25th Anniversary
articles.summary: Thorpe Park is launching Tenement, a fully immersive pitch-black scare maze for its 2026 Fright Nights event, in which guests navigate darkness with a shared, gradually failing light source. The concept leans into sensory deprivation and shared jeopardy rather than elaborate sets, offering a relatively low-cost but high-impact design model. FEC operators running haunted attractions or escape room experiences may find the mechanics of this concept worth adapting.

articles.title: Movie Park Germany Goes All-In on IP-Driven Horror for Halloween 2026
articles.summary: Movie Park Germany's Halloween Horror Festival 2026 is anchoring its season around a new Jason Universe horror house under the theme 'Legends Never Die,' leaning heavily into film IP to drive attendance. The strategy illustrates how parks and FECs are using recognizable horror franchises to justify premium ticket pricing and generate advance buzz. Operators planning seasonal horror events can draw lessons from the IP licensing and marketing approach.

articles.title: PortAventura Expands Halloween Season with New Horror Experiences and Family Programming
articles.summary: PortAventura World is extending its 2026 Halloween season from September 19 to November 15, introducing new scare attractions alongside family-friendly programming to broaden its audience reach. The dual-track strategy of adult horror and family fun reflects a growing industry norm for maximizing seasonal event revenue across demographic segments. FEC operators running fall events should note the extended run dates and mixed-audience programming model.

articles.title: LEGOLAND New York's Brick or Treat Returns as a Family Halloween Model
articles.summary: LEGOLAND New York Resort's Brick or Treat Halloween event returns October 2, featuring trick-or-treating, live entertainment, and LEGO character meet-and-greets in a fully family-friendly format. The event is a strong example of how parks and FECs can capture Halloween season traffic without relying on scare-based content. Operators targeting families with young children can reference this as a programming template for fall engagement.

articles.title: Accessibility and Inclusion Are Good for Business, Not Just Good Ethics
articles.summary: A column from the Big Break Foundation argues that diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) initiatives in the attractions industry are revenue-positive strategies, not just moral obligations. The piece presents practical framing for operators who may be hesitant to prioritize accessibility investments. FEC operators expanding venues or refreshing programming should consider how inclusive design translates to broader market reach and guest loyalty.

articles.title: Siam Park Reports 20% Attendance Boost from Nighttime Summer Event
articles.summary: Siam Park saw a 20 percent increase in attendance during its eight-week Siam Night festival, which transformed the water park into a moonlit festival environment after dark. The results underscore the strong revenue potential of after-hours events that extend operational hours without requiring major capital investment. FEC operators with underutilized evening capacity should look closely at this nighttime event model.

articles.title: Fairytale Farm's Illuminated Evenings Showcase the Value of Seasonal Nighttime Events
articles.summary: Fairytale Farm in Oxfordshire is bringing back its Illuminated Evenings event for autumn 2026, running Friday through Sunday from late October to mid-November with a new Wonderland light experience. The event demonstrates how smaller family attractions can generate incremental revenue through low-overhead seasonal programming. FEC operators of any size can draw inspiration from the format's simplicity and family appeal.

articles.title: Attractions.io Builds Guest Navigation App for Mexico City's Massive Bosque de Chapultepec
articles.summary: Attractions.io has partnered with Bosque de Chapultepec, a sprawling 866-hectare park in Mexico City, to develop a mobile app that helps guests navigate across four sections with limited phone signal. The project tackles wayfinding, day planning, and real-time orientation at scale, offering lessons for any multi-zone FEC or entertainment campus. Operators managing large or complex venues should pay attention to how mobile technology is being used to solve navigation and guest flow challenges.

articles.title: Why Designers Must Challenge Their Own Expertise to Drive Innovation
articles.summary: A Blooloop opinion piece uses the parable of five monkeys to argue that the most dangerous place for an attraction designer is inside their own expertise, where unchallenged assumptions calcify into outdated practices. The piece encourages operators and designers to bring in outside perspectives and question inherited processes. For FEC operators planning redesigns or new attraction additions, this is a timely reminder to audit assumptions before committing to familiar formulas.

articles.title: Future-Proofing Theme Parks: How to Stay Relevant Across Changing Generations and Social Norms
articles.summary: The piece explores how theme and amusement park operators must evolve their offerings not just to match current guest preferences but also to retire content that has become outdated or culturally insensitive. It notes that content once considered acceptable can become a liability as social norms shift, with real examples from the park industry. FEC operators curating themed environments, characters, or narrative experiences should treat this as a useful risk-management and long-term programming guide.

articles.title: Bob Rogers' DEEP STORY Framework Offers Creators a Roadmap for Emotionally Resonant Experiences
articles.summary: DEEP STORY, a new book by themed entertainment veteran Bob Rogers, provides step-by-step case studies and techniques for connecting audiences emotionally through immersive experiences. For FEC operators investing in escape rooms, dark rides, or story-driven attractions, the methodology offers a structured creative foundation. The book is positioned as a practical tool for anyone building transformational guest experiences rather than just entertaining ones.

articles.title: TEA Announces 2026 Masters Inductees Honoring Themed Entertainment Innovators
articles.summary: The Themed Entertainment Association has revealed its 2026 TEA Masters inductees, recognizing professionals whose careers have made lasting contributions to the global attractions industry. The annual program spotlights designers, engineers, producers, and craftspeople whose work advances innovation across themed entertainment. FEC operators and suppliers can use the inductee list as a guide to industry thought leaders and emerging best practices.

articles.title: American Wave Machines and China Tourism Group Launch Surf Park Joint Venture
articles.summary: American Wave Machines and China Tourism Group have formed Eastern Swell Dynamics, a joint venture to expand PerfectSwell surf pools across China using CTG's extensive tourism and real estate infrastructure. The deal signals growing institutional investment in surf parks as mainstream entertainment attractions in Asia. FEC investors and operators considering surf or water attractions should track this partnership as an indicator of where capital is flowing.

articles.title: Experience UK Launches Steering Groups to Shape Future of Visitor Attractions Trade Body
articles.summary: Experience UK has created three new membership steering groups, Experience Creators, Experience Operators, and Place Shapers, to give industry voices a formal role in guiding the trade association's priorities. The structure is designed to improve collaboration and ensure programming reflects real operator challenges and opportunities. UK-based FEC operators and suppliers should consider engagement with these groups as a way to influence industry policy and access peer networks.

articles.title: ETC Releases Improved Hybrid Processor for Live Event and Attraction Lighting Control
articles.summary: ETC has added an upgraded HPU+ hybrid processor to its Hog hardware family, featuring a simplified mechanical design that improves serviceability and road durability. While aimed broadly at live events, the product is directly relevant to FEC operators running theatrical lighting in escape rooms, haunted attractions, laser tag arenas, and immersive experiences. The improved serviceability could reduce downtime and maintenance costs for operators relying on sophisticated lighting control systems.
